stem: Sam is a 16-month-old infant admitted overnight with his first episode of wheeze. He has improved with salbutamol and is being discharged on salbutamol 4-hourly. Which device is the most appropriate for administering his reliever medication at home?

options.text: Pressurised metered-dose inhaler (pMDI) with a spacer and face mask

explanation: For a 16-month-old child, the preferred reliever delivery device is a pMDI used with a spacer and face mask. Young children cannot coordinate inhalation with a pMDI alone, and nebulisers are not usually needed for routine home use after improvement.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part A

rationale: The original item was a matching/order question. It has been converted to a single-best-answer item focusing on the most appropriate inhaler device for a 16-month-old child.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. This is the preferred and most practical device for toddlers and infants.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect. A young child cannot reliably coordinate use without a spacer and mask.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect. Dry powder inhalers require an adequate inspiratory flow and are not suitable at this age.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. Nebulisers are generally reserved for more severe episodes or when inhaler therapy is not feasible.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect. Oral salbutamol is not the preferred route for acute asthma/wheeze management.
